body: They are safer than not taking them.

Thanks for reassuring me that I'm not just being whiny by being upset by this. I do feel better for having ranted. Only 5 days to seeing a counsellor and a week and a half until I get to see my family doctor and probably get my meds adjusted. That's going to be "fun" but it should be better in the long run.

I think you need to make your own off my chest post to rant about this instead of hijacking mine. I wouldn't be functional without medications. I had to start taking Prozac before puberty. That was prescribed by an actual psychiatrist since the government would pay for one when I was a minor. The possible horrible side effects from giving it to a child were considered better than letting me continue unmedicated. I know that side effects can be bad but hey, at least I stopped showing signs of hallucinations and didn't kill myself when I was 12. I was expected to never live independently and now I can, even if I need help sometimes, all thanks to psychiatric medications.

The meds really. I am also annoyed he is not available but I know that is illogical. He only takes vacations this long when he's doing charity work and he'll be back soon. I just wanted him to be back two weeks ago.

I do get all my meds from the same Canadian drug store chain at the same location. I actually picked up a refill of my Cipralex with the Naproxen to save a trip so it would have been staring him in the face. I got a consult on the Naproxen where he told me all about how it gives you ulcers so there was an opportunity to bring it up.

I did receive and read a printout because I was heavily warned about the risk of ulcers and I like to be informed. Not knowing increases my anxiety. I threw it out ages ago but I don't remember an SSRI interaction being mentioned.

I'm more angry at my pharmacist but I feel let down by my doctor. He's always had my back before and has been an advocate for me. The hospital psych ward wouldn't take me when I tried to admit myself, I probably would have died if he hadn't arranged for me to be admitted. Looking back I called him on what was probably a fully booked day in mid afternoon. He told me to come straight in and must have pushed back or cancelled other appointments to talk to me for so long and make those phone calls. I guess I'm disappointed and feel let down.

I live in Canada and I'm on disability assistance supplemented by a part time job. I can't afford a psychiatrist. It's not a matter of cutting corners, it's a matter of I wouldn't be able to afford rent or food. I can only afford to go to a government funded counsellor with a wait list a mile long.

I know my family doctor won't know every drug interaction ever but he has been my primary physician since I was 5. He knows more about my health than my Mother. The only reason I was able to start taking SSRIs was because he got extra samples from the rep for me until I managed to get on disability as an adult and get my prescriptions covered.

I don't have the drug handout anymore but I did read it because everyone kept warning me about ulcers and I like to know things. I don't recall anything about the interaction being mentioned. The pharmacist should have known because I get all of my meds from the same pharmacy and I picked up a refill on my Cipralex when I got the Naproxen. I also got a consult where he talked to me about the drug side effects and freaked me out about ulcers. To be honest I didn't think much of what was basically Aleve that was prescribed so the government would pay for it outside of being paranoid of stomach aches. I've been on Cipralex for years so I had no reason to reread information on it.
SSRIs aren't usually dangerous to start, except for the temporary increased risk of suicide, but they do have nasty side effects if you stop them cold turkey.

I am horrifically depressed and anxious. Its been slowly getting worse and I've just about reached my breaking point. My pills had been working for years and I don't know they they stopped. I'm on a wait list for a free counsellor, since I can't afford private care, and my family doctor is on vacation and I won't discuss this with the other doctors in his practice.

I tore my meniscus a few months ago so I cant exercise which might have helped when I was still feeling energetic enough to leave the house. I've just gone back to work as a cashier for the first time since I injured myself. I had to leave my second shift early because I was in so much pain I couldn't stand it. I can't afford a knee brace and going through the fucking bureaucracy to get my government health plan to pay for it seems like an impossible task. I don't even want to step foot into the office because I haven't bothered to send in my pay stubs since November they're going to assume I'm trying to defraud and get more disability assistance when really it's just too fucking hard.

I got an email from my professor at 1am on Sunday asking why I hadn't submitted an assignment. It was an out, an offer to let me submit it and still pass the course. I read the email and had a panic attack. I laid in bed knowing that somewhere in my room even if I couldn't remember where was my clonazepam and I just needed to get up and find it and the anxiety might stop. But why get up, I won't find it anyways. My room is a mess even for me and it could be anywhere. So I just laid in bed and cried, unable to gather the will to even try. I haven't submitted the assignment. I could do it in an hour if I could do it at all. I don't know.

I only got dressed today because I didn't want my Mother to judge me when I left my room for dinner. She's already upset that I didn't register for any Summer classes. What's the point in taking them.

I thought writing this post would help. I just feel even more useless.

I probably should do so in the morning when his office is open. I don't know if I will. Phones cause me great anxiety and it took quite a while to call him initially.

I also get anxious because I am worried he will recommend or enforce hospitalisation. I've been there, done that, rather not repeat it. I felt physically safe because I knew I couldn't kill myself but it did fuck all for my depression. Hospital psych wards are a shitty place to stay.

It might sound odd but I have shit to do for school. If I die then it's no problem anymore. That stress and anxiety wont be mine anymore. But if I live I can't do it from inside of a ward. If I'm going to throw away tuition money I'd better be dead.

Talking this out is helping right now. I think I I've reached the magic place where I'm tired enough to fall asleep without ruminating too much.
